questions: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?

turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.agentText:
Now let's check the responses.ts `stream()` method and the Responses API's ResponseStream, plus beta threads/runs streaming and how `_client.post` with `stream:true` routes into `Stream.fromSSEResponse` inside the core client.I now have enough to give a complete, well-evidenced answer.

## Streaming implementation

**Core SSE engine — `src/core/streaming.ts`**
- `Stream<Item>` class (line 21): wraps a `fetch` `Response` as an `AsyncIterable<Item>`.
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse()` (line ~24): parses Server-Sent Events, JSON-decodes each `data:` payload, stops at `data: [DONE]`, throws `APIError` on `{error: ...}` payloads.
- `Stream.fromReadableStream()`: alternate constructor for newline-delimited JSON streams (used for browser/backend passthrough, e.g. `ChatCompletionStream.fromReadableStream`).
- `_iterSSEMessages()` / `SSEDecoder` / `iterSSEChunks()`: low-level SSE line/byte parsing shared by all resources.

**Wiring point — `src/internal/parse.ts`, `defaultParseResponse()`**
This is where *every* streaming request actually gets turned into a `Stream`: if `props.options.stream` is true, it calls `Stream.fromSSEResponse(...)` (or a custom `options.__streamClass` if set) instead of doing a normal `response.json()`. `APIPromise` (`src/core/api-promise.ts`) uses `defaultParseResponse` as its default parser, so any resource method that does `this._client.post(url, { ...body, stream: true })` transparently resolves to `Stream<Item>`.

**Higher-level streaming wrappers (event-driven helpers), all built on `Stream`:**
- `src/lib/EventStream.ts` — generic base class (`EventStream<Events>`) providing `.on()`, async iteration plumbing, abort handling.
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` — `ChatCompletionStream` (extends `AbstractChatCompletionRunner`), accumulates `ChatCompletionChunk`s into a snapshot, emits `content`, `content.delta`, `chunk`, tool-call events, etc. Static entry: `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion()`.
- `src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` — `ResponseStream`, accumulates Responses API events via `accumulateResponse()` (`src/lib/responses/ResponseAccumulator.ts`). Static entry: `ResponseStream.createResponse()`.
- `src/lib/AssistantStream.ts` — `AssistantStream` for the (deprecated) Assistants/Threads/Runs API, emits `messageDelta`, `runStepDelta`, `toolCallDelta`, etc. Static entries: `AssistantStream.createAssistantStream()`, `createToolAssistantStream()`.
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts` — streaming variant of the tool-calling "Runner" (auto function-calling loop over a stream).

## Public API methods that route into streaming

| Method | File | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `client.responses.create(body /* stream:true */)` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:96-123` | `this._client.post('/responses', { stream: body.stream })` → raw `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` |
| `client.responses.retrieve(id, { stream: true })` | same file, ~135-165 | same mechanism, GET `/responses/{id}` |
| `client.responses.stream(params)` | same file, `stream()` method | delegates to `ResponseStream.createResponse()` (event-driven wrapper) |
| `client.chat.completions.create(body /* stream:true */)` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:~62-78` | `this._client.post('/chat/completions', { stream: body.stream })` → raw `Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(params)` | same file, `stream()` method | delegates to `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion()` |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools(body)` when `body.stream` | same file, `runTools()` | delegates to `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.runTools()` |
| `client.completions.create(body /* stream:true */)` (legacy Completions API) | `src/resources/completions.ts` | same `post(..., { stream: true })` pattern → `Stream<Completion>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create(threadId, params /* stream:true */)` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:~15-33` | `post(..., { stream: params.stream, __synthesizeEventData: true })` → raw `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.stream(threadId, body)` / `.createAndStream(...)` | same file | delegates to `AssistantStream.createAssistantStream()` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.submitToolOutputs(runId, params /* stream:true */)` | same file | raw `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.submitToolOutputsStream(...)` | same file | delegates to `AssistantStream.createToolAssistantStream()` |

All of these bottom out at the same place: `_client.post/get(...)` sets `options.stream = true` in the request options → `APIPromise` resolves via `defaultParseResponse` (`src/internal/parse.ts`) → `Stream.fromSSEResponse()` (`src/core/streaming.ts`). The `lib/*Stream.ts` classes are convenience wrappers around that raw `Stream`, not separate transports.

**Not verified:** `src/realtime/*` (WebSocket-based streaming for the Realtime API) — I did not open `realtime/index.ts`, `realtime/websocket.ts`, or `realtime/ws.ts`, so I can't confirm whether/how they reuse `core/streaming.ts` vs. an entirely separate WS event-emitter path. Also did not verify `src/resources/videos.ts`/`containers.ts` for any additional streaming endpoints, and did not run/execute any code — this is a static-read analysis only.
